title: Daily Market Digest: October 8, 2026
subtitle: Market closes lower as rising oil prices and hawkish Fed signals weigh on sentiment.

items.headline: U.S. Equities Decline Amid Surging Oil and Rising Treasury Yields
items.summary: U.S. stock indices closed lower on Thursday, October 8, 2026, as investors grappled with rising crude oil prices and elevated Treasury yields. This combination fueled inflation concerns and reinforced expectations for further hawkish monetary policy from the Federal Reserve. The broad market sentiment was notably defensive, with particular pressure on technology and other rate-sensitive sectors. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Wolfspeed Soars on Defense Loan Commitment
items.summary: Wolfspeed Inc. ($WOLF) saw significant gains, rising 19.86% to $37.60 in after-hours trading after receiving a $1.5 billion conditional loan commitment from the U.S. Department of Defense.

items.headline: Haemonetics Posts Strong Intraday Rally
items.summary: Haemonetics Corp ($HAE) climbed 17.52% to $119.61 by late morning, making it one of the day's top performers.

items.headline: PepsiCo Rises on Earnings Beat
items.summary: PepsiCo Inc. ($PEP) shares rose 1.92% to $126.10 after the beverage and food giant surpassed Wall Street's third-quarter earnings and revenue expectations.

items.headline: Levi Strauss Falls on Revenue Miss
items.summary: Levi Strauss & Co. ($LEVI) stock fell 3.1% after the company reported stronger profits but revenue growth that fell short of analysts' expectations for its latest quarter.

items.headline: Marvell Technology Under Pressure Amid AI Caution
items.summary: Marvell Technology ($MRVL) shares dropped approximately 2% as investor caution grew around artificial intelligence (AI) stocks and the broader semiconductor sector faced headwinds.

items.headline: Oracle Declines with Broader Tech Weakness
items.summary: Oracle Corp ($ORCL) declined 1.65% as the technology sector experienced broader weakness during Thursday's trading session.

items.headline: Energy Sector Leads as Tech Lags on Thursday
items.summary: The Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund ($XLE) was a top performer, rising 2.79% on the back of surging crude oil prices. Conversely, the Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund ($XLK) lagged, declining 0.46%, reflecting a broader shift in market sentiment. Consumer Staples ($XLP) also showed strength, gaining 1.34%.

items.headline: Fed Officials Signal More Rate Hikes Likely by Year-End
items.summary: Minutes from the Federal Open Market Committee's (FOMC) September 15-16 meeting, released yesterday, indicated that most officials anticipate another interest rate increase by year-end to combat persistent inflation. Today, Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller reiterated that additional rate hikes will likely be needed but noted 'flexibility' regarding the pace, possibly allowing for a pause at the upcoming October meeting before a potential December hike.

items.headline: Oil Prices Surge, Treasury Yields Remain Elevated
items.summary: Brent crude prices jumped above $104 per barrel, up around 3.8%, driven by escalating geopolitical tensions and hurricane-related production disruptions in the U.S. Gulf. Concurrently, the 10-year Treasury yield hovered near 5.33%, close to its highest level since 2002, increasing borrowing costs and impacting equity valuations.

items.headline: Weekly Jobless Claims Indicate Continued Labor Market Strength
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Labor's weekly Initial Jobless Claims report for the week ending October 3, 2026, was released today. Fewer Americans applied for unemployment benefits than expected, suggesting a resilient labor market.

items.headline: Helen of Troy Delivers Strong Q2 Earnings and Optimistic Guidance
items.summary: Helen of Troy Ltd. ($HELE) exceeded second-quarter earnings estimates, reporting $0.79 per share against expectations of $0.51, a 54.9% positive surprise. Strong guidance for the current quarter and full year led to a significant pre-market rally for its shares.
